final.memo:
We have examined the company and its role in supplying network infrastructure [D01]. While the company is currently profitable, its business model requires constant technological innovation and frequent acquisitions to remain relevant in a rapidly changing industry [D01], [D05].

We prioritize businesses with durable competitive advantages that we can understand and project with high confidence over the long term [D05]. Because this company's economics are tied to a volatile technological cycle, we are unable to determine its long-term intrinsic value [D05].

We avoid businesses that require constant, unpredictable capital expenditures or perpetual acquisitions to maintain their position [D05]. Consequently, this investment sits firmly in our 'too hard' pile, and we prefer to keep our capital in assets with more certain long-term prospects [D05], [D08].
